Topics · Who was Muhammad?

How do I tell a true messenger from a false one?

Three questions for anyone speaking for God: how he lived, what he calls to, what grew. Each has a limit.

Part 1 of 3

﴿إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ١٠٧ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ١٠٨ وَمَآ أَسْـَٔلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ١٠٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger. So fear Allāh and obey me. And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.

Quran · Ash-Shu'ara 26:107-109

Translation

Here I am. Witness against me before Yahweh and before his anointed. Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I defrauded? Whom have I oppressed? Of whose hand have I taken a bribe to make me blind my eyes? I will restore it to you.” They said, “You have not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither have you taken anything from anyone’s hand.”

Original · Hebrew

הִנְנִ֣י עֲנ֣וּ בִי֩ נֶ֨גֶד יְהוָ֜ה וְנֶ֣גֶד מְשִׁיח֗וֹ אֶת־שׁוֹר֩ ׀ מִ֨י לָקַ֜חְתִּי וַחֲמ֧וֹר מִ֣י לָקַ֗חְתִּי וְאֶת־מִ֤י עָשַׁ֨קְתִּי֙ אֶת־מִ֣י רַצּ֔וֹתִי וּמִיַּד־מִי֙ לָקַ֣חְתִּי כֹ֔פֶר וְאַעְלִ֥ים עֵינַ֖י בּ֑וֹ וְאָשִׁ֖יב לָכֶֽם׃ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ לֹ֥א עֲשַׁקְתָּ֖נוּ וְלֹ֣א רַצּוֹתָ֑נוּ וְלֹֽא־לָקַ֥חְתָּ מִיַּד־אִ֖ישׁ מְאֽוּמָה׃

1 Samuel · 12:3-4

World English Bible

﴿ٱتَّبِعُوا۟ مَن لَّا يَسْـَٔلُكُمْ أَجْرًا وَهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Follow those who do not ask of you [any] payment, and they are [rightly] guided.

Quran · Ya-Sin 36:21

Translation

I coveted no one’s silver, gold, or clothing. You yourselves know that these hands served my necessities, and those who were with me.

Original · Ancient Greek

ἀργυρίου ἢ χρυσίου ἢ ἱματισμοῦ οὐδενὸς ἐπεθύμησα· αὐτοὶ γινώσκετε ὅτι ταῖς χρείαις μου καὶ τοῖς οὖσι μετʼ ἐμοῦ ὑπηρέτησαν αἱ χεῖρες αὗται.

Acts · 20:33-34

World English Bible

Start with the person before the message. A fraud wants something: money, rank, followers, a name. So ask two things of anyone who speaks for God. What was he known for before he made the claim? And what does he take from the people who believe him? These sentences set that as a public test: a man calls himself trustworthy in front of those who know him, and says he asks no wage. His hearers could check both.

A question for you

When someone speaks in God's name, what would you look at first?

If you sayWhat he gains from it.
ThenThat is the oldest check there is, and it catches many frauds. It can miss a sincere person who is mistaken, and that is a separate question.
If you sayHow he lived before the claim.
ThenThat is a record others can report on. Its limit is that you depend on the people who kept it, so you will want to know who they were.
If you sayNothing about him. Only whether what he says is true.
ThenThat is a fair start, and the next part takes it up. A person's record cannot make a false teaching true, or the reverse.

Part 2 of 3

﴿مَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُؤْتِيَهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلْحُكْمَ وَٱلنُّبُوَّةَ ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ كُونُوا۟ عِبَادًا لِّى مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَـٰكِن كُونُوا۟ رَبَّـٰنِيِّـۧنَ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تُعَلِّمُونَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ وَبِمَا كُنتُمْ تَدْرُسُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

It is not for a human [prophet][134] that Allāh should give him the Scripture[135] and authority and prophethood and then he would say to the people, "Be servants to me rather than Allāh," but [instead, he would say], "Be pious scholars of the Lord because of what you have taught of the Scripture and because of what you have studied."

Translator's notes

[134] Or any believer. [135] Or in the case of Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ), "the Book" (i.e., the Qur’ān) .

Quran · Aal Imran 3:79

Translation

When Peter entered, Cornelius met him, fell down at his feet, and worshiped him. But Peter raised him up, saying, “Stand up! I myself am also a man.”

Original · Ancient Greek

ὡς δὲ ἐγένετο τοῦ εἰσελθεῖν τὸν Πέτρον, συναντήσας αὐτῷ ὁ Κορνήλιος πεσὼν ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας προσεκύνησεν. ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Ἀνάστηθι· καὶ ἐγὼ αὐτὸς ἄνθρωπός εἰμι.

Acts · 10:25-26

World English Bible

Now the message. Three things can be asked of it. Does it point to the Maker of all things, or back to the speaker? Does it call to justice, mercy and honesty, or only to loyalty? Does it sit well with what is best in a person, or does it ask you to silence your conscience? This sentence draws the sharpest line of the three. Whoever is truly sent does not turn people toward himself.

A question for you

Which message would you trust least?

If you sayOne that makes its messenger the centre.
ThenThen you have a test that cuts across every tradition, including what is offered here. Use it evenly.
If you sayOne that asks me to silence my conscience.
ThenThen conscience has a vote for you. The open question is what to do when conscience and a text seem to differ.
If you sayOne that flatters me and my people.
ThenA message that tells its people only what they like to hear costs them nothing. That is worth noticing in any book, including the one you were raised with, if there was one.

Part 3 of 3

﴿أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَسَالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌۢ بِقَدَرِهَا فَٱحْتَمَلَ ٱلسَّيْلُ زَبَدًا رَّابِيًا ۚ وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِى ٱلنَّارِ ٱبْتِغَآءَ حِلْيَةٍ أَوْ مَتَـٰعٍ زَبَدٌ مِّثْلُهُۥ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَضْرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْحَقَّ وَٱلْبَـٰطِلَ ۚ فَأَمَّا ٱلزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَآءً ۖ وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَضْرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْأَمْثَالَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

He sends down from the sky, rain, and valleys flow according to their capacity, and the torrent carries a rising foam. And from that [ore] which they heat in the fire, desiring adornments and utensils, is a foam like it. Thus Allāh presents [the example of] truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it vanishes, [being] cast off; but as for that which benefits the people, it remains on the earth. Thus does Allāh present examples.

Quran · Ar-Ra'd 13:17

Translation

Truth’s lips will be established forever, but a lying tongue is only momentary.

Original · Hebrew

שְֽׂפַת־אֱ֭מֶת תִּכּ֣וֹן לָעַ֑ד וְעַד־אַ֝רְגִּ֗יעָה לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר׃

Proverbs · 12:19

World English Bible

Last, what came of it. Given time, does a message leave people more honest, more merciful, more just, or does it burn off? This image is a flood. Foam rides high on the water and then vanishes, and what is of use stays in the ground. The test is slow, and it has a flaw: success alone proves little, since false causes also win for a time. So the question is not whether it spread. It is what stayed, and whether people were better for it.

A question for you

If you were judging a message by what came of it, what would you look at?

If you sayWhether it spread.
ThenMany things spread, for many reasons, so this measure says little alone. That is why size is not offered as evidence here.
If you sayThe best people it produced.
ThenThat is the fairest place to begin: those who follow it most closely. The question after that is how far this can be trusted.
If you sayWhat ordinary followers are like today.
ThenThat is a real thing to weigh, and it includes Muslims as much as anyone. It measures the followers, which is not always the same as measuring the teaching.

The same in the other books

Translation

Now I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. When I heard and saw, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel who had shown me these things. He said to me, “You must not do that! I am a fellow bondservant with you and with your brothers, the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God.”

Κἀγὼ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀκούων καὶ βλέπων ταῦτα. καὶ ὅτε ἤκουσα καὶ ἔβλεψα, ἔπεσα προσκυνῆσαι ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ποδῶν τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ δεικνύοντός μοι ταῦτα. καὶ λέγει μοι· Ὅρα μή· σύνδουλός σού εἰμι καὶ τῶν ἀδελφῶν σου τῶν προφητῶν καὶ τῶν τηρούντων τοὺς λόγους τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου· τῷ θεῷ προσκύνησον.

Whose word do you take on something that matters, and what did they do to earn it?
